clue.text: Girl soldiers embracing a carrier

indicators.note: embracing means the soldiers' letters wrap around the carrier's

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, stands for soldiers
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A young woman's regiment escorts a vehicle or porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' is the container signal; RA, the Royal Artillery, is a crossword staple for soldiers, and 'a' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female first name, so it is an example of a girl.

clue.text: Unsophisticated Oriental novelist

parts.note: green means naive or inexperienced
E is short for eastern

explanation.surface: A naive writer from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was an English writer of novels such as Brighton Rock.

clue.text: Settler in America is looking wan

explanation.surface: A pioneer in the New World looks sickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: In Westerns, Native Americans call a white settler by this term; and someone with a pallid complexion looks washed out.

clue.text: Are able to dance, but only for a spell

parts.note: are able means can
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: People can dance, but only for a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like a period of time; here it is a magic charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a witch's charm or magical incantation.

clue.text: Makes up orders

explanation.surface: Someone invents and arranges things.
explanation.definitionFit: To write music or verse is to create it; to arrange things in their places is to put them in order.

clue.text: Public relations unity may reveal bias

parts.note: oneness means being united as a single whole

explanation.surface: A publicity drive for togetherness may expose prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency or inclination toward something is a leaning, like a prejudice.

clue.text: The cleaner coloured, framing the French quack

indicators.note: framing means the cleaner and coloured pieces sit either side of the French article

parts.note: a char is a British word for a cleaning lady
tan means coloured brown, as by the sun
la is the French feminine form of the

explanation.surface: A suntanned cleaning lady flanks a French woman who sells fake medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framing' is the container signal, with the cleaner and colour pieces on either side. A char (charwoman) is a British cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A quack is a fraud claiming medical skill, a type of impostor.

clue.text: A firm supporter, but a crawler

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a bra supports the bust

explanation.surface: A loyal backer who turns out to be a sycophant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests a toady; here it is a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous snake, which moves along the ground on its belly.

clue.text: Borne by the female aphis in spring

indicators.note: borne by means the letters are carried inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A greenfly hatched in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season; it is a jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A jump or bound into the air.

clue.text: A fan might be there and in a frenzy

indicators.note: in a frenzy says the letters of there and and are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: A frantic enthusiast might be at the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a frenzy' rearranges THEREAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower or supporter of a cause or person.

clue.text: Once coppers finish, pay out

parts.note: ex means former, once
P is pence, copper coins
end means finish

explanation.surface: When the police are done, settle the bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coppers' looks like police; here it means small coins, pence.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money is to lay it out.

clue.text: Guided a Spartan queen

parts.note: led means guided

explanation.surface: Someone escorted a royal from Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was wife of King Tyndareus of Sparta and was visited by Zeus as a swan.

clue.text: Carol's after a single member-nothing special

indicators.note: after places the carol's letters at the end

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
O looks like zero, nothing
to carol is to sing; the 's means is

explanation.surface: A carol follows one politician, nothing remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing special' reads as one phrase, but 'nothing' gives O and 'special' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand and impressive stands out as out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Augment control on violence

parts.note: rein means to control, as with a horse
force means violence

explanation.surface: Increase restraint on brutality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen something by adding more support.

clue.text: The children outside got agitated

indicators.note: outside means the children's letters go around the word the

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical usage

explanation.surface: The children were upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' is the container signal; seed is an old, biblical word for descendants or offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: To boil with anger or excitement is to be stirred up.

clue.text: They'll support the board

parts.note: reads like company backers of a board of directors, but means the frames that hold up a tabletop

explanation.definitionFit: Trestles are A-frame supports on which a board rests to form a table.

clue.text: Have the sheriff's assistants go by ship

parts.note: a posse is a group summoned by a sheriff
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Get the deputies to travel by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to hold it as one's own.

clue.text: Take too much dope and do ever so badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of do ever so are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone takes too many drugs and fares terribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges DOEVERSO.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume an excessive and dangerous amount of a drug.

clue.text: Drink, having the wind up?

explanation.surface: A drink taken when nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having the wind up' means being frightened; read literally, it is air blowing upward, as a current up a chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: A swallow of liquid is a gulp; a current of air passing through a room or flue is a breeze.

clue.text: Corset-an essential for the older person

indicators.note: essential treats corset and an as the raw substance from which, reworked, the word is made

explanation.surface: A girdle is a must for an elderly person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential' is an unusual anagram signal: CORSETAN rearranged is the essence of the answer. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is someone from an earlier generation of one's family.

clue.text: Row with anybody joining

explanation.surface: An argument with anyone who joins in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a rank of seats. 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is a rank or layer; one who ties or knots things is someone fastening them together.

clue.text: One in seven is from men vying for top jobs

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: One in seven is among men competing for top posts.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven are the seven deadly sins.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Few irritate when really macho

parts.note: VI, six in Roman numerals, stands for a small number
rile means irritate

explanation.surface: Few people annoy a genuinely tough man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Few' gives VI, six, as a small number; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Manly and strong, full of masculine vigour.

clue.text: May well be eager to give assent

indicators.note: may well be says the word eager could be a rearranged form of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone keen to say yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May well be' rearranges EAGER; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To say yes or consent to a proposal.

clue.text: A charge made by agitated Tories

indicators.note: agitated says the letters of Tories are stirred up

explanation.surface: An attack mounted by angry Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' rearranges TORIES, members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden attack made by troops from a defensive position.

clue.text: Still in the minority

parts.note: reads like being outnumbered, but minority means the legal state of being a child

explanation.definitionFit: Too young legally, not yet having reached adulthood.

clue.text: A means of fixing wages

explanation.surface: A way of rigging pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixing' suggests rigging; it means fastening. Screw is British slang for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded metal fastener; and slang for a salary or pay.

clue.text: The mason, though ill, cheers wildly

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of ill and cheers are thrown about

explanation.surface: The stoneworker, though sick, applauds wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges ILLCHEERS; 'though' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone mason works with a cutting tool, a chisel, so is one who carves.
